name: Scan for Each Matching Character
summary: For every character in s, linearly scan t for the first equal character that has not already been consumed. Fail if any source character cannot claim a match.
visualizationIntent: init: show s and t as aligned character rows with all t positions unused. loop: the source pointer selects one character while the candidate pointer scans all of t. update: a matching unused t cell turns green and becomes unavailable. return: false when no candidate remains, otherwise true after every source character is matched.

lineExplanations.3: Initialize the verdict from the length comparison.
lineExplanations.4: Check whether unequal lengths already disprove an anagram.
lineExplanations.6: Track which t positions are already consumed.
lineExplanations.7: Start with the first source character.
lineExplanations.9: Assume no match has been found yet.
lineExplanations.10: Start scanning t from the beginning.
lineExplanations.12: Compare the source and candidate characters.
lineExplanations.13: Check whether the candidate is unused.
lineExplanations.14: Accept only an equal unused candidate.
lineExplanations.16: Record that this source character matched.
lineExplanations.17: Stop scanning t for this source character.
lineExplanations.18: Advance to the next t candidate.
lineExplanations.19: Check whether the full t scan failed.
lineExplanations.20: Record that no valid anagram exists.
lineExplanations.22: Advance to the next source character.
lineExplanations.23: Return the true verdict after every character matched.

syntaxExplanations.2: def isAnagram(self, s, t): receives two strings.
syntaxExplanations.3: answer = len(s) == len(t) stores whether the lengths match.
syntaxExplanations.4: if not answer: detects unequal lengths.
syntaxExplanations.5: return answer reports the false length verdict.
syntaxExplanations.6: used = [False] * len(t) creates one availability flag per t character.
syntaxExplanations.8: while i < len(s): processes every source character.
syntaxExplanations.9: found = False resets this source character's result.
syntaxExplanations.11: while j < len(t): scans all candidates.
syntaxExplanations.12: same = s[i] == t[j] compares the characters.
syntaxExplanations.13: available = not used[j] checks whether t[j] is free.
syntaxExplanations.14: if same and available: requires both conditions.
syntaxExplanations.18: j = j + 1 advances to the next candidate.
syntaxExplanations.19: if not found: detects a failed full scan.
syntaxExplanations.20: answer = False stores the failed verdict.
syntaxExplanations.21: return answer reports a missing match.
syntaxExplanations.22: i = i + 1 advances the source index.
syntaxExplanations.23: return answer reports that all characters matched.
